parts.technique: E(X) of a discrete random variable
parts.reason: S4.1 explicitly excludes 'calculation of mean and variance of discrete random variables'; this question requires finding E(X) for a discrete random variable, which is exactly the excluded content.

parts.label: a
parts.reason: Completing a tree diagram with probabilities is covered by S3.1/S3.2 guidance on tree diagrams.

parts.label: b
parts.reason: Finding P(water) using total probability from a tree diagram is standard S3.2 content.

parts.label: c
parts.reason: Using P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B) for independent events is explicitly in S3.1.

parts.label: d
parts.reason: Uses conditional probability formula P(A|B) and solving simultaneous equations from tree diagram, covered by S3.2.

parts.label: e
parts.reason: Finding P(F|W) and comparing probabilities uses conditional probability formula from S3.2; depends on parts (a)-(d) but those are in spec so this is fine.

parts.label: a
parts.reason: Finding a probability using the Normal distribution as a model is covered by S4.2.

parts.label: b
parts.reason: Finding a value given a probability using the Normal distribution (standardising and inverse) is covered by S4.2.

parts.label: c
parts.reason: Combines conditional probability (S3.2) with Normal distribution calculations (S4.2), both in spec; no excluded content involved.

parts.label: d
parts.reason: Finding probability of at least one success in repeated independent trials, calculable via binomial distribution (S4.1) or direct complement using independence (S3.1); no mean/variance of discrete RV required.

parts.label: a
parts.reason: Identifying outliers using 1.5×IQR rule is explicitly covered in S2.4 guidance.

parts.label: b
parts.reason: Drawing box plots including outliers is covered by S2.1 guidance (box and whisker plots including outliers).

parts.label: c
parts.reason: Describing skewness using quartiles is standard S2.3 measures of variation/central tendency interpretation content.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Redraw box plot with new outlier limits
parts.reason: Same as (b), redrawing a box plot with new quartiles/outliers is covered by S2.1/S2.4.

parts.label: e
parts.reason: Drawing inferences about data values from changes in quartiles is covered by S2.4 guidance on drawing inferences from measures of central tendency and variation.

parts.label: a
parts.reason: Explicit exclusion S2.2: 'calculations involving regression lines are excluded'; this part directly requires substituting into a regression equation.

parts.label: b
parts.reason: Calculating Sxx/Syy from summary statistics is covered by S2.3 (Sxx formula and standard deviation from summary statistics), extended analogously to Syy; not itself a regression-line calculation or PMCC formula use.

parts.label: c
parts.reason: S5.1 explicit exclusion: 'Students will be expected to calculate a value of r using their calculator but use of the formula is not required' and S2.2 excludes correlation coefficient formula calculations; this part explicitly requires calculating Sxy then r via formula, which is the excluded method with no calculator-only alternative offered in the mark scheme.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Sxy algebraic reasoning with regression line data
parts.reason: This requires manipulating Sxy formula in context of an 11th data point added to a regression dataset; while it's an algebraic argument, it is intrinsically a 'calculation involving regression lines' context excluded by S2.2, and depends on the excluded Sxy/regression machinery.

parts.label: e
parts.reason: Explicitly a calculation involving/deriving a regression line equation, excluded by S2.2.

parts.label: f
parts.reason: Commenting on extrapolation/suitability of a regression line is part of S2.2 guidance ('dangers of extrapolation') which is allowed interpretive content even though calculations with regression lines are excluded; this part requires no calculation, only interpretation.

parts.label: a
parts.reason: S4.1 explicit exclusion: 'calculation of mean and variance of discrete random variables is excluded'; this asks to show E(A) for a general discrete random variable.

parts.label: b
parts.reason: Directly excluded by S4.1 exclusion on calculation of variance of discrete random variables.

parts.label: c
parts.reason: S4.1 guidance explicitly states students should know and identify the discrete uniform distribution.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Symmetry argument for E(B) of discrete uniform distribution
parts.reason: Although framed via E(B)=E(A), the mark scheme accepts a symmetry argument for the discrete uniform distribution rather than requiring calculation of E(X); however it fundamentally relies on E(A) from the excluded part (a) and the concept of E(X) for discrete RVs, which S4.1 excludes.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Comparing Normal distribution probabilities using given μ,σ
parts.reason: Given values of μ and σ directly (not derived via excluded mean/variance calculation), finding/comparing P(X>3.5) is a Normal distribution probability calculation covered by S4.2.

parts.label: f
parts.technique: Normal distribution probability with chosen extreme parameters
parts.reason: This part only requires selecting the largest possible μ (=7) and smallest possible σ (=1) directly from the given tables of values of A and B (not via any excluded E(A)/Var(A) calculation), then standardising and finding a Normal probability, which is core S4.2 content; it does not depend on the excluded parts (a)/(b) since μ and σ are read directly from the distribution tables of A and B.

parts.label: g
parts.technique: Probability of specific discrete outcomes (A=7 and B=1)
parts.reason: Uses independence of two discrete events P(A=7)×P(B=1), covered by S3.1 independent events; does not require excluded E(X)/Var(X) calculation, only reading probabilities from given tables.
